panels.title: Invalid feed entities skipped
panels.description: GTFS-RT entities dropped because they have no usable id or entity type.

panels.title: Invalid entities skipped (range)
panels.description: Total invalid GTFS-RT entities skipped in the selected range.

panels.title: Feed age since last success
panels.description: Static feeds poll every 5 minutes and have a 10-minute timeout. Warn at 10 minutes, page at 30.

panels.title: Static ingestion attempts by outcome
panels.description: Every attempt, including unchanged, rate-limited, timeout and failed.

panels.title: Archive download duration (average)
panels.description: Mean time to transfer an archive, summed over all feeds. A 304 Not Modified does not transfer or record a duration.

panels.title: Static cycle duration (average)
panels.description: Wall-clock time for one scheduled polling cycle across every feed.

panels.title: Static cycles skipped (range)
panels.description: Cycles skipped because the previous cycle was still running. A nonzero value means 5 minutes is too tight.

panels.title: Archive size (largest observed)
panels.description: Peak of the Micrometer max gauge over the range. The gauge decays, so this is not the exact histogram maximum.

panels.title: 304 Not Modified polls
panels.description: Polls resolved without transferring an archive. A feed that stops revalidating is suspicious.

panels.title: Feed registrations configured vs reporting
panels.description: Each app registers every feed it is configured for, so both series count app/feed pairs. A gap means an app has not attempted one of its feeds yet, so no age gauge exists.

panels.title: Database write rate
panels.description: Writes per second by table operation.

panels.title: Flush duration (average / max)
panels.description: Total time to map and persist one drained batch.

panels.title: Duplicate updates dropped
panels.description: Duplicate trip updates and database-rejected updates.

panels.title: Flush phase duration
panels.description: Map time versus each database operation, so the slow half of a flush is visible.

panels.title: Stored delay source
panels.description: Stop-time rows by where their delay_seconds came from: published by the feed, derived from the static plan, or none.

panels.title: Rows without a delay by feed

targets.expr: sum by (feed) (rate(gtfs.sink.delay{application=~"$application", feed=~"$feed", source="none"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (feed) (rate(gtfs.sink.delay{application=~"$application", feed=~"$feed"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.description: Share of rows stored with a NULL delay_seconds. A high share means the feed cannot be tied to the static schedule.

panels.title: Static lookup duration (average / max)
panels.description: Time to read the static stops a flush needs for sequence resolution and delay derivation.

panels.title: Static stops loaded per flush
panels.description: Static stop rows loaded per flush; only the stops the batch refers to are read.

panels.title: Off-heap load ratio
panels.description: Hash table occupancy. Sustained values near 1 trigger a resize.

panels.title: Validation outcomes
panels.description: Valid, invalid, checksum mismatch, fetch failure, malformed event and disabled outcomes.

panels.title: Outcomes by feed (range)
panels.description: A table, not a flat time series: increase over the whole range is a single value per feed/result.

panels.title: Violations by feed and file (range)
panels.description: Violation counts over the selected range, per feed and file.

panels.title: Max violations per archive
panels.description: The worst single archive in the selected range.

panels.title: Event age at processing start
panels.description: Time between archive publication and the start of processing.

panels.title: Persistence revisions by result
panels.description: Loaded, unchanged, failed and disabled persistence outcomes.

panels.title: Persistence load duration (average)
panels.description: Time to stream a validated archive into the database.

panels.title: Rows written per second by table
panels.description: The per-table counters are monotonic, so this is a write rate; the total rows per load is above.
